html:
SMTO-SKL-0183 — Your GitHub request stopped before it finished

GUID: 1a3c2743-e8dd-5afe-944e-37ebaf63fb79
Slug: github-operation-cancelled
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • The GitHub request stopped partway, either because the Run was stopped or because GitHub took too long to answer. Steps that finished before that still happened on GitHub; the rest did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the Run's activity in this conversation to see which GitHub steps finished before it stopped. Steps that completed before the stop still took effect on GitHub.
  2. Open the relevant issue, pull request or release on github.com to confirm what is there now. Checking GitHub directly avoids repeating a change that already happened.
  3. If you still want the rest done, ask the Agent to continue with only the remaining steps. If you didn't stop the Run, check github.com is working first. Asking for only what's missing prevents duplicate comments, issues or uploads, and a slow GitHub can stop the request again.

What success looks like

  • The Agent finishes the remaining steps and each change appears once on github.com.

If it still fails

  • If it stops again without you stopping it, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The GitHub skill observed cancellation (task cancellation, or its socket owner cancelled, which also happens when a single GitHub response exceeds the 60-second socket deadline) before the next request or between response chunks; requests completed earlier still took effect, and a write already sent is reported separately as outcome unknown.

What this means

  • GitHub cancellation is observed before another request or at a transport checkpoint; in-flight mutation failures have separate uncertainty handling. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • GitHub cancellation is observed before another request or at a transport checkpoint; in-flight mutation failures have separate uncertainty handling.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the last receipt and whether any earlier write was dispatched.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the receipts of earlier GitHub calls in this Run and the current state on GitHub, then request only the remaining work. If a write had already been sent, handle it under github.mutation_outcome_unknown (or the specific outcome-unknown error) and reconcile it before any new write.
  • Inspect prior receipts and resume only deliberate remaining work; reconcile any already-dispatched uncertain mutation first.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Deliberate continuation starts from reconciled provider state.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
